findings.reason: the search should have named the existing member-axis owner before new batch types were authored, so the plan either extended it or justified a second one.
findings.text: the survey's "Concrete scope for Nova's next plans" recommends building the ensemble coupled forward without citing nova's own `nova/transport/ensemble.py`, whose `EnsembleForwardTransport`/`EnsembleTransportState`/`EnsembleTransportReceipt` (landed 2026-08-20, commits c792f7d2c and cc542659c) already implement identity-preserving member batching and are documented as "the batched member form" in `nova/transport/AGENTS.md:19`

findings.reason: a second member-axis family drifts from the owner while carrying the same identity contract, and the plan should extend `nova/transport/ensemble.py` or state why the window payloads cannot use it.
findings.text: `MemberArrayBatch` and `BatchedWaveform` re-implement the typed identified leading member axis (member_ids validation, read-only freezing, identity-based `member()` lookup) that `nova/transport/ensemble.py:51-116` already owns as `EnsembleTransportState`, and `WindowMemberReceipt`/`WindowBatchReceipt` (window_batch.py:271-334) duplicate `EnsembleMemberReceipt`/`EnsembleTransportReceipt` (ensemble.py:137-161)

findings.reason: two live copies of the window convergence policy mean a change to one silently diverges from the other, and the plan should extract a shared per-member exchange-step policy or extend `solve_window`.
findings.text: `solve_window_batch` copies the convergence control policy of `solve_window` (`nova/transport/coupled_window.py:1413-1515`): the convergence-receipt construction, the conservation-residual check, the four-way refusal decision (hard ceiling / contraction unavailable / stalled at floor / cap needs measurement), the halving damping backoff, the continuation sampling and the blend are reproduced line-for-line in the per-member loop

findings.reason: the batch genuinely needs a per-member refusal carrier that names the member identity, so wrapping the owner's typed errors is a reasonable extension.
findings.text: `WindowRefusalReason`/`WindowMemberRefusal`/`WindowBatchError` introduce a refusal taxonomy beside the existing `WindowConvergenceError`/`WindowConservationError` (`nova/transport/coupled_window.py:1183`, raised at :1490) rather than extending the owner's error family

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — `solve_window_batch` hides the entire batched fixed-point exchange, host-side receipt assembly and fail-closed per-member refusal behind one call, and `observation_kernels` hides units/COCOS/support/error receipts behind three functions.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — `nova/transport/window_batch.py` re-implements the identified leading member axis and its identity receipts already owned by `nova/transport/ensemble.py`, and `solve_window_batch` copies the convergence/backoff/ceiling policy owned by `solve_window` in `nova/transport/coupled_window.py`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; no section adds a CLI option, MCP views or refusal family, and the additions are Python symbols inside the transport and equilibrium modules.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan's cross-repo survey searched the ambix estimator machinery but not nova's own existing batched-member module `nova/transport/ensemble.py`, which already owned the member-axis batch contract three days before the plan's batch work landed.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §3's virtual flux-loop and probe kernels compose the existing `nova.biot` loop/probe factories and `sample_chord_psi_norm` and add a measured error bound and a receipt the factories lack.
